Collaboration is central to my research because challenges involving water quality, landscape resilience, sustainable food production, and environmental decision-making cross disciplinary and institutional boundaries.

## Current research setting

I am based at the University of Guelph, where my work connects geography, environmental science, agriculture, water resources, and food systems. My current research builds from precision conservation and watershed management toward a broader program on resilient agricultural landscapes and sustainable food production.

## Established collaborations

My research has developed through collaboration with universities, Environment and Climate Change Canada, conservation authorities, agricultural and environmental organizations, NGOs, international development organizations, and private-sector partners. These partnerships connect scientific research with operational environmental management and implementation.

## Future collaboration interests

<ul class="interest-list"><li>Earth Observation and Agricultural Remote Sensing</li><li>GeoAI and Spatial Environmental Intelligence</li><li>Agricultural Water Quality and Watershed Science</li><li>Precision and Multifunctional Conservation</li><li>Long-Term Environmental Monitoring</li><li>Climate-Resilient Agricultural Landscapes</li><li>Environmental Economics and Spatial Optimization</li><li>Decision-Support Systems and WebGIS</li><li>Food-System and Agricultural Resilience</li></ul>

I welcome collaborations involving research projects, grant proposals, comparative studies, datasets, graduate student research, and applied environmental initiatives.
